scope: Killybegs James: a tax balance and a working Donegal father

prior_assessments.basis: Select Thomas Glasgow-3556 of Lifford/Raphoe as the uncertain working father of James Glasgow-3001. Thomas is an established Donegal legal/property actor from the 1684 Raphoe-linked court occurrence through the 1692–1695 Shannon/Ballindrait deeds and the 1701 Exchequer continuation. James belongs to a later dated Donegal account under 1728. The same uncommon surname, regional continuity and compatible succession of legal/property and revenue roles make Thomas a useful preferred existing father account. This extends the recorded Ramelton–Lifford family into the otherwise unattached collector account without inventing an intermediary. It is a regional and generational inference: none of these records names James as Thomas’s son.
prior_assessments.limitations: The record dates are not measured ages. The 1728 entry may carry an earlier deceased or dismissed officer’s balance, so it cannot select a generation precisely. Archibald Glasgow-1101, Thomas’s probable father, remains a concrete older-family alternative: James might be Thomas’s younger brother or another kinsman rather than his son. An unrelated Donegal or wider Ulster Glasgow family remains possible. The Tyrone James Glasgow-1025 and Belfast Captain James Glasgow-3172 are not merged with this collector or excluded solely by their unproved birth estimates and parent fields. No Scottish-to-Irish migration, exact age, mother, spouse or child of James is inferred. Thomas’s existing probable Archibald father and his other children keep their separate assessments.
